session.title: 从智能到行动 ：东南亚AI落地实践

summary:
东南亚正处于AI规模化落地的关键节点。论坛汇聚区域企业领袖，共同探讨一个核心命题：企业如何从探索智能、走向规模化部署AI行动？
通过与行业先锋、技术构建者与内容创作者的深度对话，论坛将从基础模型、基础设施、智能体应用延伸至创意经济，完整呈现AI落地的全貌。与会者将获得东南亚AI转型的一手洞察、理解区域发展趋势、把握布局先机。

segments.title: Qwen家族炉边对谈：游戏、连接服务与AI银行的不同落地阶段
segments.summary: Adeline Toh Ying Ying主持Anna Kuzmenko、Dedy Handoko、Nic Ngoo，讨论Razer的游戏AI探索、CBN连接客户的增值产品路线，以及Ryt Bank客户对话交易和内部工程应用，比较生产路径、客户KPI及日常工作流对规模化的作用。
key_points: Razer介绍QA Companion和Ava数字伙伴方向，强调与游戏开发者、玩家和创作者合作；明确仍在不同模型探索阶段，不写成Qwen全部成熟生产收益
CBN以约9000企业与70万零售连接客户为基础寻求AI增值，Digital Worker、GenAI Token网关及Enterprise AI Suite为接下来产品路线
Ryt Bank自述基于阿里云构建，150万客户中40%使用对话AI，累计逾1200万AI交易；拍账单识别和意图核实简化支付，均为该银行现场口径
Ryt Bank客户询问响应运营减少90%、70%代码AI生成属于指定内部业务指标，不当成全部银行运营或岗位减少
Ryt向300余员工提供Qwen Coder和QoderWork，约50活跃使用，案例含信贷材料总结与安全日志分析；不是全员深度采用
完全自主银行、MCP及Agent互通、自愈基础设施仍在探索测试
最后建议有侧重：CBN逐客户明确收入效率KPI，Nic要走出POC循环并建立生产路径，Anna解决真实业务问题并嵌入日常工作流

segments.summary: Ang Kai Loong分享Touch n Go电子钱包的AI采用，把辅助工具、AI增强流程、复杂任务团队分成三个阶段，以QA自建工具和数据仓库分析说明当前实践，并以可见性、易用支持和安全治理培养AI素养，反思过早限制模型与预算带来的采用阻力。
key_points: 受监管且面向消费者的组织背景，2700万认证用户为讲者自述规模
公司目前分处工具辅助和AI增强流程两阶段；端到端复杂任务由Agent形成假设并研究原因是目标阶段
初级QA通过QoderWork生成图片测试工具及自然语言写入沙箱测试用户，使用者可自建小工具
数据分析插件当前可自行写执行SQL、继续分析并交人复核；自主回答流失原因并决定测试仍为未来方向

paragraphs.text: All right, good afternoon. I'm from the data and AI division from TNG Digital Malaysia

blocks.display_note: 画面主体为Ang Kai Loong，声音按原始语义turn分别归属。

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: and our division we drives AI adoption in the company. So what I'll be doing here today is to share with you our AI adoption journey. Now, first we have a quick glance of our business.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: TNG Digital runs Touch 'n Go e-wallet in Malaysia. And for context, Malaysia has 33 million population and we have 27 million verified users. And we are in payment, finance, travels, daily services like mobility tools, merchant services, so on and so forth.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: So in our case, AI adoption is an AI adoption in a regulated and consumer-facing organization.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now, AI literacy. 20 years ago, organizations stopped hiring managers who couldn't use computer. And in a very near future, I believe that it will be the same with AI. Now AI has become a basic skill and it's a skill that the more you use, the more uses you find and the more benefit you get.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: And that skill is the literacy. Now, technology can be bought, but literacy has to be built. And this is how we build it.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Our company, we are looking at three stages. Now, in stage one, we are looking at AI as your tool. So everyone gets a copilot, you use to write email, draft this that, and do analysis in a faster manner.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: you do the work and AI assist. And this is part of my company is, and this is where most of the companies are today. Well, stage two, which is another half of my company is at, is where your AI augments your process, where you designed the work around AI, now AI does the routine work and humans check the result.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: For example, in my team, we build data pipelines using AI and we have humans or engineers to check it before going live. And last stage where we want to be, AI as your team, where we wish to delegate complex end-to-end tasks to the agent.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: For example, you can ask a question to the agent, why did the customer churn increase last month? And we want the agent to do the analysis, come back with the results, and we will act out of it.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: This is where we want to be. Now next, I'll be sharing at our current stage what we have built, these cases.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: this is a stage one, is a QA specific use case. now, when it comes to software QA, software testing, there's always a need for small utility tools. and every time they need it, basically, it needs to go to a request to the developer team to build it, or the QA would allocate a time to build it themselves.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: But most of the times, these tools, they are not built because it's time consuming. And then the QA would just work around manually. Now, with AI, in our case, we're using Qoder and QoderWork.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: the QA, we just have to describe the problem to the AI tool and then you get the working tool, the utility tool on the same day. now this example here, they are exact use cases by our junior QA using QoderWork.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: now on the left, we were testing a feature where we require users to upload a photo and the system has to cope with whatever comes in. Wrong format, huge file, blur, rotated template, and so on and so forth.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now, before AI, what we had to do, we had to look for samples and then edit them by hand, one by one, manually. Now today, what the QA did, she just told the AI, the QoderWork, her problem.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: And the AI come out with a tool. And this makes testing much faster. And on the right, there's another use case where we are testing a feature that behaves differently depending on the user category, region, and also their KYC status.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now to test this properly, you need a lot of combinations. Hence, you have to do a lot of accounts creation. Again, before AI, you have to create this one by one or you have to have someone to do the automation for it.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: So what the QA did again, she described the problem to the AI and the AI built a tool that takes in natural language and write in all these test data to the sandbox system for testing.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now, with just one sentence, the QA typed in, you know, I want 50 users split into three categories and with expired KYC and then this data are generated and pump into the system.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: it saves a lot of time. now, neither of these examples, they are not impressive engineering. and that's the point. now, the people who needed the tool are now the people who could build it.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Next one, which is our stage two example, our data warehouse AI analytics agent. This one, there are three stages, if you map it out, and right now we are stage two, but let's go with stage one.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now, when ChatGPT first came out, and if you are in the data department or division, you must have seen this behavior before, where you take the information of a data set from your data warehouse, copy into the AI tools, and ask the AI tools to generate the SQL statement, and then you copy paste this thing back to your data analytics platform,

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: run the queries, get the result. And then you copy this back into the ChatGPT and then do analysis and then the ChatGPT when it wants to do further analysis. It asks you to do another SQL, you know, again and again.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Okay, that was stage one. Right now, we are in stage 2 where we could tell AI what we want to analyze. for example, we want to know what is the customer trend by region. the AI would work out how it would write the queries itself, run the queries itself, checks, further analyze it, and give the result,

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: and we review it. and that's the plugin that we built, and that's where we are right now. And where we want to head towards is we don't just want to ask what, we want to ask why.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Again, using the same example, why did the customer churn increase? We would like the agents to decide what to look at, what hypothesis to form, what tests to do, do everything by itself, come up with the result and then you review it.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: And that's where we're heading towards. now for these two use cases, neither of these came from a roadmap. they are built by people who just know how to use AI tools. and these are the people that we want to build in the organization.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: and how do we build it? three pillars. first, make AI visible. show people what's possible with AI. so two things that we did here, we had workshops, we have our service providers, we have alibaba cloud came in.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: To one workshop to show people how to use QoderWork and take on some real case, real life example and work it out. And we have our AI Showcase Day where each division that have their people coming out to demo their AI use cases.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now the second pillar is to make it easy. Three ways we make it easy, three levels. First is by having data and AI stewards. We have champion in every division and those people are fluent in AI and they will teach their teammates how to use AI.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: The second level where our team act as consultants, the business unit will come to us and then we give our consultation and they themselves build it. This would be for simplest project.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now the third one was a bit more complex. We have our Forward Deployed Engineers that would be joining the project, sitting with the business unit, figure out their problems, And build the solutions with them.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now third one, the Safety Pillar where we have our AI Council that sets the direction and rule telling us, what you can do with AI, what you cannot do with AI. And the people in the AI Council, they are Data and AI, Tech and Risk.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now with these parties, every perspective needed, they are in the room so we can move faster. and safer.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: and yeah, what we got wrong? okay. now, managing cost was right, but managing cost in a very tight manner and doing it before fluency was built, that was a mistake. and that's what we learned.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: so what we did, we told people to use a weaker, cheaper models for simple tasks, everyone. and then we even looked into restricting top-tier model usage. and from day one, we set a very tight budget per person, and we got the budget wrong.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: we under-budgeted it. So what happened? The non-technical users, which they are the majority, they couldn't tell apart what is a simple task, what is a complex task. And also to make it worse, with the budget limit, they just opt for the cheaper and weaker model.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: So naturally, AI failed most of the tasks, and they concluded AI doesn't work. Now, and also the budget ran out mid-cycle, hence the adoption slow down for a period. So what we learned is beginners that need the best model, not the cheapest.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Now, experts that could work around with weak models, but beginners can't, and majority of them are beginners. Hence, limits should come after fluency, if budget allows. And we do track our usage per person within monthly to better manage the budget moving forward.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: Right.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: With this, so in order to adopt AI, so three things I would do, you know, put a council in place, give people the best model, and start asking people and helping them to build a new workflow around AI step by step.

paragraphs.speaker: Ang Kai Loong
paragraphs.text: And that's all my presentation. Thank you.

segments.summary: Ananda Budi Prasetyo与Galih Permadi、Dennis Sze、Dong Shou讨论通用方案不足的业务原因，以及Lapis AI定制模型与上下文、Advance AI身份风险和Ren3主权Agent编排实践。讨论数据积累、治理控制、模型组合和长期维护，并从业务KPI与系统位置判断自建采购。
key_points: Lapis AI从系统集成走向定制SaaS，Relay叠加Model Studio，按任务组合模型、微调及Qwen VL与YOLO；强调结果准确与迭代优化，不承诺一次即最佳
Galih把语言差距进一步解释为上下文管理：结构化非结构化知识、Ontology和客户上下文工程比单纯模型大小重要
Advance AI反深伪和注入攻击需持续追赶欺诈者，自研模型及云上训练推理仍持续投入，不写成欺诈问题已彻底解决
主持引用Allo Bank约75万验证用户及Bukalapak75%自动验证为客户案例；Dong说明500多客户积累的行业欺诈模式及投入摊薄价值
Advance AI从业务起点使用阿里云印尼基础设施以满足当地数据主权需求，为实际部署陈述
Ren3从首日内建谁可用、访问哪些数据、在哪运行、何时做什么及付出多少成本的控制，兼顾技术债与可持续性
主持40%成本下降、30%质量提升为引用案例；Dennis介绍不同任务组合模型、成本时长延迟可见和持续调优，模型路由是接下来能力
区域差距各有侧重：Dong数据基础与独有积累，Galih上下文和本体，Dennis失败反馈及控制经验
对CTO建议：持续维护学习与自建采购取舍，明确AI用于OLTP自动化或OLAP分析，先定业务问题和收入成本KPI

segments.title: 创意圆桌：从多模型工作流到本地IP商业化
segments.summary: Ngoi SeKeng主持Arsifa Deliyana、Ivan Tan、Pax Chen、Tao Santimakorn，讨论平台聚合与长视频资产管理、AI降低实验成本、OPC合作和新型文化IP，以及内容安全、注意力与差异化。各方从实际产品经验走向微IP、数字分身、院线与去中心化创作展望。
key_points: Videfly从用户短期流失反思工具堆叠，按创作目标与企业工作流定制、白标或代制作，人工仍参与；数字人模板先人工设计并检查与现有人物相似性
Loomi Imaginary面向长视频组织角色道具场景资产，结合3D与视频参考控制镜头及动作，工具工作流价值超出单模型渲染
T&B强调AI降低试验成本，可先发布测试内容观察观众反应；速度之外真正稀缺的是注意力、内容差异和信任
Fizzdragon以全球创作者及OPC共创自有IP，探索热点、老年社区故事、文旅互动电影及IP收益合作；全球首部电影是嘉宾自称，不作外部认证
Loomi以云端内容过滤、专业用户KYB、后台扫描及分发链路把关；Videfly数字人概念设计和相似性检查为实际过程，不扩张为法律保证
对质量深度，Pax认为新创作者可探索艺术风格并沉淀Skill，传统制作者与AI共同演进；主持强调互补
Deli建议数字分身是个人未来建议；Tao预期微IP与微短剧并重人才再培训和IP跨行业，时间判断为展望
Loomi已有商业微短剧，后续计划扩展院线、漫画转视频与东南亚超本地内容；Pax主张分散创作并做传统产业难覆盖的新机会
最后总结文化、价值和故事决定区域差异，创新工具降低创作门槛同时保留人的创造作用
